g.title: N17 [Method: ReAlign] (cites=0) ReAlign. Building on the geometric analysis in Sec. 3, we introduce ReAlign, a training-free pre-alignment strategy that maps text representations into the image representation distribution using statistics derived from large-scale unpaired data.

g.text: ReAlign operates through a three-stage procedure.
g.title: N17pre [Method] (cites=0) ReAlign operates through a three-stage procedure.
N17a [Method: Anchor-component] (cites=0) First, Anchor Alignment matches first-order statistics (means).
N17b [Method: Trace-component] (cites=0) Second, Trace Alignment matches the global variance scale.
N17c [Method: Centroid-component] (cites=0) Finally, Centroid Alignment explicitly rectifies the geometric drift induced by spherical projection.

N17d [Method] (cites=0) Together, these stages achieve precise cross-modal alignment at the statistical level using only linear transformations and normalization, without requiring any additional training.

g.text: ReVision. We incorporate ReAlign into a two-stage MLLM training
g.title: N18 [Method: ReVision] (cites=0) ReVision. We incorporate ReAlign into a two-stage MLLM training pipeline termed ReVision.

N18a [Method: ModSubPretrain-component] (cites=0) In the first stage, Modality Substitution Pretraining, the ReAlign operator is used to convert large-scale long-form text into pseudo-visual representations.

N18b [Method: AdapterTrain-component] (cites=0) An adapter is trained on these representations while keeping the LLM backbone frozen, enabling the model to absorb rich world knowledge and visual semantics purely from text data, without relying on costly image–text pairs.

N18c [Method: VisInstrTune-component] (cites=0) In the second stage, Visual Instruction Tuning, real images are introduced for standard supervised learning to supplement fine-grained visual details that may be lost under purely statistical alignment, thereby refining the model's ability to follow complex instructions.
